title: Sovereign failover lockdown and verifiable evidence automation for Private/VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable an enforceable 'sovereignty lockdown' for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that prevents automated failover to non-approved regions except under explicit, auditable escalation. Provide an automated evidence generation pipeline that produces signed, tamper-evident audit bundles (logs, topology, TLS cert fingerprints, KMS-signed timestamps) for every residency decision and any forced evacuation action. This ticket covers policy enforcement, admission/placement controls, failover gating logic, and the evidence export API and retention lifecycle so Security/Legal can demonstrate compliance to customers and auditors.
background: Customers in regulated industries require that workloads tagged as 'sovereign' never leave allowed geographic boundaries except under documented emergency procedures. Current control plane allows failover to compatible regions when capacity is constrained, but we lack: (1) per-deployment enforceable lockdown flags that halt automatic cross-region routing, (2) an auditable approval flow for exceptional failovers, and (3) a compressed, signed evidence bundle for retention and export. Several enterprise conversations and recent RFPs referenced the need for tangible audit artifacts and an approvals trail.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Policy flag `sovereignty.lock=true` can be set at deployment/org level and prevents automatic region failover from the control plane.
A2: Attempting to initiate an automatic failover to a region not in the deployment's allowlist returns a blocked response and emits a detailed audit event with geo-tags.

A3: There is an operator-approved escalation flow: an authorized principal can request emergency failover; request is recorded and requires a signed approval via console or API; approval, reason, and TTL are included in the evidence bundle.

A4: Evidence bundle for each failover decision (blocked or allowed) includes timestamped, KMS-signed entries: placement decisions, route tables, KV cache snapshots (prefixes redacted), involved host metadata (region, AZ), and config hashes. Bundles are stored encrypted and accessible via audit API for at least 90 days by default.

A5: Unit and e2e tests cover webhook enforcement, policy evaluation, and evidence signing; CI includes an integration scenario where a staged load triggers a blocked failover and an approved emergency failover and verifies bundle contents.
A6: Documentation in Confluence (link in attachments) describes operator steps, RBAC controls, and retention defaults; product PM has signed off on UX for approval flow.
A7: Metrics emitted: attempts_blocked_total, emergency_approvals_total, evidence_bundles_generated_total; alerts configured when blocked attempts > 5 in 1h for a single customer.
A8: Backwards compatibility: customers without `sovereignty.lock` flag maintain current behavior; feature flag gated rollout for 2 weeks.
A9: Security review completed and SRE runbook for emergency manual evacuation published.
A10: Performance: policy check adds <10ms median latency to placement decision path in the happy path.
A11: Compliance export supports on-demand signed bundle creation and scheduled daily snapshots for tenants that opt-in.
A12: Evidence retention lifecycle respects customer-configurable retention settings with a minimum of 30 days and admin-settable up to 7 years.
implementation_notes: Introduce a `sovereignty` boolean and `allowed_regions` list on Deployment resource; persisted in control plane DB with immutability rules unless change uses explicit approval flow.
Add admission webhook in the Private control plane that rejects any placement or routing mutation that would leave allowed_regions unless an emergency_approval token is present and valid.
Policy engine: extend existing placement policy evaluator to consult deployment-level flags before computing alternative regions. Keep decision path functional and cacheable for hot requests.

Evidence pipeline: create evidence-builder microservice that subscribes to placement/audit topic, collates related logs, signs bundle with customer-specific KMS thumbprint, compresses and stores to encrypted object store (S3 or on-prem equivalent).
Approval UX/API: console endpoint to request emergency failover; owners list validated via org RBAC (SSO groups). Approval issues a short-lived signed JWT (TTL-configurable) to pass through webhook.
Retention/exports: wire retention settings to lifecycle manager; provide audit API endpoint allowing export of bundle(s) for a given time window; include checksum and signature verification endpoint.
Testing: create an integration harness that simulates capacity loss in primary region and ensures blocked behavior and approval flow operate as expected; include simulated network partition cases.
Observability: add tracing spans across policy evaluation and evidence generation; expose per-tenant metrics and dashboards in Console; add alerting rules in PagerDuty for suspicious patterns.
Telemetry & privacy: redact PII and token content from evidence bundles by default (configurable), log redaction steps in bundle metadata.
Operational playbook: on-call steps to manually generate and sign bundles if evidence service is degraded; documented in runbook and linked in attachments.
Rollout: feature-flagged release to select pilot customers for 2 weeks before wider rollout; gather feedback and watch for latency/false-blocking.
Performance optimization: precompute policy outcomes for common configurations and warm caches in the runtime to keep added latency under 10ms.
KMS integration: use per-customer envelope keys if available; otherwise use company-managed signing key with ACLs and audit logging in KMS.
Compatibility: make sure Private on-prem air-gapped deployments can produce evidence bundles and store them locally; evidence exporter supports local NFS/S3-compatible endpoints.
Data model: store bundle manifest in control plane DB with fields (bundle_id, tenant_id, created_at, regions_involved, approval_token_id, retention_expiry) as flat columns.
Backfill: migration plan for existing deployments to default `sovereignty.lock=false`; allow bulk opt-in tooling for enterprise tenants.
Security: threat model review required prior to GA; ensure PKCS7 signatures or equivalent are used for tamper-evidence.
Legal: include consent language for evidence exports in customer agreements (PM to coordinate).
Deps: coordinate with SRE (for runbooks/alerting), Security (for KMS and signing), and Console (for approval UX).
Developer notes: prototype at github.com/redwood-inference/infra/priv-residency-proto (link below).
risks: R1: Overblocking could cause customer outages if allowlist is misconfigured; need clear error messaging and escalation.
R2: Evidence bundle size could grow large for long incidents; must bound snapshots and allow selective inclusion/exclusion.
R3: Key management complexity when supporting per-customer signing keys; operational overhead and rotation must be automated.
R4: Air-gapped/on-prem deployments may not have a managed KMS; fallback signing approach must be secure and documented.
R5: Latency impact on placement decisions if evidence collection is synchronous; design to do signing asynchronously where possible while still recording reason deterministically.
R6: Legal/contractual implications if we permit forced evacuation under emergency; PM/legal involvement required to define acceptable emergency scenarios.
R7: Integration testing surface is large (control plane, runtime, console, KMS, object storage, retention worker) — plan for staged rollout and strong CI coverage.
R8: Potential for audit data to contain sensitive identifiers; must ensure redaction and strict access controls.
R9: Requirement for a human-approval channel introduces operational latency; need to tune TTLs and fallback behaviors.
R10: Malicious actor could try to trigger many blocked attempts to generate noise; add rate-limiting and fraud detection.
R11: Interplay with existing autoscaling and Dedicated capacity policies; ensure we don't conflict with capacity priority rules.
R12: Retention costs for long-lived evidence required by some customers could be non-trivial; provide pricing guidance.
R13: Synchronization across multiple control planes in multi-region private installs could be complicated — require coordination protocol.
R14: Edge cases when a region is partially degraded (some AZs) — need clear policy for partial evacuation.
R15: Need clear migration story for existing customers and a way to audit historical placement decisions into new bundle format.
R16: CI secrets exposure risk when generating signed bundles in test environments; use test KMS keys and separate storage.
R17: Verification tooling must be provided for auditors to validate signature chain; otherwise bundles are less useful.
R18: Upgrades to control plane while lockdown is active must not inadvertently change allowlist semantics; upgrade gating required.

decision_log: D1 (2025-02-19): Use KMS-signed manifests for tamper-evidence; per-tenant keys optional. Agreed: signatures must be verifiable externally via public key endpoint.

D2 (2025-02-25): Evidence generation will be async with deterministic reason recording synchronously to avoid increasing placement latency. A deterministic decision record will be persisted synchronously, full bundle generated asynchronously.
D3 (2025-02-27): Approval tokens TTL default set to 1 hour; configurable by enterprise admin up to 24 hours.
D4 (2025-02-28): Redaction default policy: remove PII and full prompt text; customers can opt-in to include more context via contract.
D5 (2025-03-01): Pilot rollout will target 3 enterprise customers that have expressed interest in the feature; choose customers across cloud and on-prem setups.
